subject: Competitive eval: model quality follow-up and next tests
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Sam Lee <sam@acme-retail.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>, Ethan Park <ethan@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Mar 2026 15:05:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap + next steps (competitive eval / model-quality prompts)

Thanks again for the call today, Sam — good to meet you and the Acme data team. Quick recap and next steps so we keep momentum on the competitive eval: 

Summary of what we agreed:
- Scope: run the same prompt set (attached) across the hyperscaler endpoint you tested and a Redwood-hosted inference run.
- Primary metrics: hallucination rate (factually incorrect assertions), precision on extraction prompts, and perplexity/fluency checks for long-context prompts.
- Target success criteria (for initial POC): hallucination rate < 5% on the fact-check suite, and parity on extraction precision +/- 3 points.

Deliverables we will provide:
- redwood_test_prompts_v2.txt (attached): canonical prompt suites — fact-checks, extraction, multi-turn context, and adversarial hallucination probes.
- A short summary PDF comparing test axes and what we recommend to surface in the CSV output (prompt, model, temp, tokens, output).

Can you send over the raw CSV you mentioned from the hyperscaler runs (prompt + model output + any logits/metadata)? That will let us do point-by-point comparisons. If you can also include the exact endpoint config (model id, temperature, max tokens, context window), that’d be great.

Proposed next steps / timeline:
1) You send the hyperscaler CSV + configs (we discussed you might have a preliminary dump) — ideally by Thu EOD PT (tomorrow).
2) We run the Redwood runs on the same prompt set and return a comparison CSV within 48 hours of receiving your samples.
3) Quick sync (30 min) after we share results to align on any follow-up tests (low-temp, high-temp, long context, tool-calling stress).

Can we tentatively book Wed 31 Mar 2026 11:00 AM PT for the sync? I’ll send a calendar hold once you confirm.

Thanks — looking forward to the data.

—
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com | (415) 555-0198
https://redwood.ai

Attachments: redwood_test_prompts_v2.txt, redwood_vs_hyperscaler_summary.pdf

From: Sam Lee <sam@acme-retail.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 26 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + next steps (competitive eval / model-quality prompts)

Thanks Marissa — appreciate the clear recap. I attached the preliminary CSV we ran against GCP’s endpoint (see acme_prelim_eval_v1.csv). Notes from our side: 

- Config: model=gcp-llm-xl, temp=0.7, max_tokens=256, context_window=8192.
- High-level: latency looks better on GCP for short prompts, but we saw elevated hallucination rates on the long-context and adversarial fact-check prompts.
- We included a "confidence" column (model-provided score) in the CSV; it's noisy and not perfectly correlated with correctness.

Two quick questions for your team:
1) When you run Redwood, can you include both our exact config and a low-temp (0.0) run? We want to see hallucination delta vs deterministic decoding.
2) Any recommended post-processing (e.g., citation heuristics) you suggest we test while we evaluate outputs?

I’ll also loop in our SRE contact if you need raw logs, but happy to start with the CSV. Sending the file now.

—
Sam Lee
Data Science Lead, Acme Retail
sam@acme-retail.com

Attachment: acme_prelim_eval_v1.csv

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Sam Lee <sam@acme-retail.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>, Ethan Park <ethan@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 27 Mar 2026 11:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + next steps (competitive eval / model-quality prompts)

Sam — got the CSV, thanks. Quick initial read and proposed additions before we run the Redwood baselines: 

Initial observations (preliminary):
- Hyperscaler (gcp-llm-xl) hallucination rate on the fact-check suite: ~9.8% (from your labels).
- From a sample of extraction prompts, precision sits ~2.5 points below the threshold you described.
- Confidence column isn’t well-calibrated on adversarial items — we see high "confidence" with incorrect outputs.

What we’ll run on our side (requested):
- Redwood variants: redwood-7b, redwood-3b, and a quantized 3b variant.
- For each model: runs at temp=0.0, 0.3, 0.7 and the same max_tokens/context as your run so outputs are comparable.
- Produce a CSV with: prompt_id, prompt, model, config, output, hallucination_label (our human-vetted sample), tokens, and simple quality flags.

Additional tests I recommend before the sync:
- Long-context stress (8k+) with repeated referential questions to surface hallucination accumulation.
- Low-temp deterministic runs (temp=0.0) to measure hallucination floor.
- Prompt-engineered variants (one-shot with explicit "verify facts" instruction).

We’ll return the Redwood CSV within 48 hours. If we see model-level regressions vs your baseline we’ll flag them and propose mitigations (scoring thresholds, citation heuristics, or fallback to smaller deterministic model for critical reads).

Confirming Wed 31 Mar 2026 11:00 AM PT works for me — please send calendar invite.

Thanks — will follow up with the comparison CSV and a short writeup on hallucination breakdowns.

—
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com

Attachments: redwood_test_prompts_v2.txt, redwood_vs_hyperscaler_summary.pdf

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>, Ethan Park <ethan@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 29 Mar 2026 11:30:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Competitive eval: model quality follow-up and next tests — internal action items

FYI / internal action list below — forwarding Sam’s CSV and our plan. See excerpts from Sam’s notes: 

> From: Sam Lee <sam@acme-retail.com>
> High-level: latency looks better on GCP for short prompts, but we saw elevated hallucination rates on the long-context and adversarial fact-check prompts.

Action items (please):
- Aditya: run the redwood-7b, redwood-3b, and redwood-3b-quant on the attached redwood_test_prompts_v2.txt across temps [0.0, 0.3, 0.7]. Produce a single CSV matching Acme’s schema (prompt_id, prompt, model, temp, output, tokens). Estimate: 24–36 hours after you have access to the CSV (I attached their file).
- Ethan: add a simple hallucination reg-check to our regression harness (prompt-based binary label + hallucination_rate metric) and wire up a dashboard alert if hallucination_rate > 6% on the fact-check suite. Also compute basic delta vs the hyperscaler baseline they provided.

Notes:
- Prioritize the fact-check suite and long-context stress tests first.
- Keep the runs deterministic and reproducible: record git commit of the loader and exact runtime config.
- If we see a model > 6% hallucination, add an immediate note in the CSV describing any obvious failure modes (e.g., timestamp drift, truncation, mis-parsed references).

We’ll reconcile results and produce the redwood_vs_hyperscaler_summary.pdf for the Wed sync. Ping me on Slack if you hit infra blockers.

—
Marissa
